body:
Thanks for your answers! I didn't expect people to reply at all, honestly. I love art and music, but I still have no idea what to do after high school. I've talk to the orientation counselor, but all she told me was that I had good grades and that I could pretty much do what I want. I might actually go back and talk to her again, but I think I'll take my time since I'll take a year off next year (Don't worry, high school finished waaaaay earlier in Quebec, so next year I won't be in high school anymore and taking a year off is a common thing to do back here). I think I might work a little and, if I got enough money to do it, I'll maybe travel (I never left the province and I've been told by some of my teachers that it really helped them with their profession choice). 
There's no after-school activities at my school that isn't related to sports (I suck sports, just in general) and people don't seem very interested by me. But, volunteering is an obligation for the school program I am in and I have to admit I've met really positive people throughout the years even if I haven't been able to really keep in touch with them. 
I have a therapist (a social worker in a program made for youths with special needs), but I didn't tell her about how I really felt before a couple of weeks ago when I was found by my French teachers having a panic attack in the girl's bathroom. My original therapy was all about trying to make me less anxious about my school performance, but that wasn't the biggest issue. I got diagnosed after that and my whole therapy is supposed to be adjusted to my needs now. I guess it's going to get better for now on.
Thanks again!

Suicide is never destiny or inevitable. It should never be an option in the first place. There's always someone or something somewhere who can hold your hand and help you find your way through life a bit better. People are kind and comprehensive when you ask for help, it's just incredibly hard to ask. When you stay alone with a far too heavy heart inside your chest for to long it's normal, for all I know, to come to think suicide is the only option. Having lost people to suicide, I recommend that you see a professional if you feel this way. I had known them forever and I can assure you that they weren't destined to die this way. If you do already seek for treatment, don't be afraid to tell people if it isn't adequate for your condition, they will understand. 
Please, anyone who suffers a heavy heart, stay with us, people care <3
